corrections.source_says: Set these three n_units values to null. The paper reports 151 human participants and 151 GPT instances, but does not report 302 as the number of analyzed observations for AUT/CT originality or elaboration. These analyses include two prompts per source; AUT reports F(1, 600) and t(602), whereas CT reports F(1, 619) and t(621). The combined count of humans and GPT instances cannot be substituted for the observation count used in those tests, and an observation count should not be back-calculated from the inconsistent degrees of freedom.
corrections.quote: To assess originality of responses via semantic distance scores, we conducted a 2 (group: human, GPT-4) X 2 (prompt: ‘fork, rope) analysis of variance.

corrections.source_says: Add the reported fluency outcome, with the matching constraint explained. AUT: humans M = 6.94, SD = 3.80; GPT-4 M = 7.01, SD = 3.81; t(602) = 0.21, 95% CI [− 0.54, 0.67], p = 0.83. CT: humans M = 5.71, SD = 3.20; GPT-4 M = 5.50, SD = 3.15; t(621) = 0.82, 95% CI [− 0.29, 0.71], p = 0.41. DAT fluency is reported descriptively in Table 2: humans 9.72 (SD 0.62), GPT-4 9.97 (SD 0.18); no DAT fluency test is reported. Fluency was matched for AUT/CT before the final validity exclusions, and the source nevertheless reports it as a scored outcome.

confirmed: Read the entire journal article as Europe PMC full-text JATS XML (PMC10858891, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10858891/fullTextXML), including Methods, Results, Tables 1-4, figure captions, Discussion, references, and back matter. No local markdown/PDF was available; the publisher PDF request returned HTML, so all source locators here are sections/tables rather than PDF pages.

source.version is supported: Scientific Reports 14, article 3440, published 2024-02-10, received 2023-10-14, accepted 2024-01-30; title and all three authors match the article metadata. The XML flags no supplement and contains no appendix (article front matter and complete body/back matter).

One empirical AI-versus-human comparison, with no randomized assignment of people to generative-AI assistance: human answers were collected via Qualtrics and GPT answers were generated separately by the first author. Counterbalanced human task order and randomly presented attention checks do not create an AI-assistance experiment (Methods > Participants; Procedure, Par29-Par30). design_class and context_class = ai_vs_human, and core = no, are correct.

The source reports 151 recruited Prolific participants and 151 GPT instances, which are not additional people. It also reports two attention-check exclusions and two DAT exclusions for fewer than seven responses, without explicitly reconciling those exclusions with the reported human N; leaving the final analyzed human count null is justified. This is not a randomized experiment with fewer than 50 people (Methods > Human participation, AI participation, and Divergent associations task, Par9-Par10 and Par28; Procedure, Par29; Table 1).

US recruitment, approval rating above 97%, English proficiency, mean age 41.21, fork/rope AUT prompts, the two CT scenarios, three-minute AUT/CT prompts, ten requested DAT nouns, and untimed DAT are supported. DAT response time 126.19 s and survey duration 34 min (SD 13.64) match the cited passages; Human participation separately prints 34.66 min for survey duration (Methods, Table 1, Par9 and Par11-Par28; Procedure, Par29).

The scoring descriptions match: AUT/CT use Open Creativity Scoring with GLoVe 840B semantic distance and stoplist elaboration; DAT averages within-list pairwise cosine distances and multiplies by 100. These are computed scores on produced responses (Methods > Divergent associations task, Par26; Results > Creativity scoring, Par33-Par34).

S1-O1: all AUT means/SDs match Table 3; group F(1, 600) = 622.10, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.51; interaction F(1, 600) = 113.80, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.16; the post-hoc p < 0.001 results and p = 0.989 exception match Results > Primary results > Alternative uses task (Par37).

S1-O2: all CT means/SDs match Table 3. The source itself repeats the AUT group/interaction F values and η2 values, with denominator df 619; retain the published numbers rather than repairing them. The post-hoc p < 0.001 results and p = 0.607 exception also match Results > Primary results > Consequences task (Par40).
S1-O3: GPT-4 M = 84.56, SD = 3.05 and humans M = 76.95, SD = 6.13; t(300) = 13.65, 95% CI [6.51, 8.71], p < 0.001 are exact reported values (Table 3; Results > Divergent associations task, Par45).

S1-O4: all recorded word counts and percentages match Par43: single occurrences 523/69.92% for humans and 152/47.95% for GPT; group-exclusive words 651/87.03% and 220/69.40%; overlap 97/9.11%. The source prints χ2(1, N = 302) = 1.56, p = 0.211, for group by word type (Par44); Table 4 gives Dog 28 and Elephant 98 as stated. Lower cross-session word variety is descriptive; that chi-square test is not a direct test of the single-occurrence percentage difference.

S1-O5: AUT elaboration M/SD 15.45/6.74 for GPT-4 versus 3.38/2.91 for humans, t(602) = 28.57, 95% CI [11.24, 12.90], p < 0.001; CT elaboration 38.69/15.60 versus 5.45/4.04, t(621) = − 36.04, 95% CI [− 35.04, − 31.45], p < 0.001 all match the source, including the CT signs (Results > Primary results > Alternative uses task, Par38; Consequences task, Par41).

The one-line finding accurately reports the direction and numerical results: nominal 1:1 AUT/CT fluency matching, greater GPT-4 originality, DAT scores 84.56 versus 76.95, and single-occurrence shares 47.95% versus 69.92% (Methods > AI participation, Par10; Table 3; Results, Par37, Par40, Par43, Par45).
This is an original empirical paper, not a synthesis; leaving study/effect counts and pooled estimates in synthesis empty is appropriate (Current research, Methods, and Results).
summary: The complete Europe PMC journal XML confirms an AI-versus-human comparison with no randomized AI-assistance study, and the existing reported result statistics match the source. Corrections concern the output-scoring eligibility flag, unsupported AUT/CT analysis counts, the DAT construct, omitted fluency results, and the missing data URL.
